 Judgment

Challenging judgment and award dated 18.02.2016 passed by V Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT-VI. Belagavi, in MVC.no.564/2012, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT-VI. Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts as stated are that in an accident that occurred on 12.01.2011, claimant while riding pillion on motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-24-J-3249, sustained grievous injuries when it met with accident with motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-24-K-4126 dashed against it.
Despite taking treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.

3. Alleging loss of earning capacity, he filed MVC.no.564/2012 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, against owner and insurer of offending motorcycle bearing registration no.KA- 24-K-4126.
4.
On service of summons, owner filed objections denying claim petition averments as false.
It was stated that vehicle was insured with insurer and liability if any should be saddled on insurer.
5. Insurer filed objections denying occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent riding of offending motorcycle by its rider.
Issuance of insurance policy was admitted subject to terms and conditions.

6. Thereafter, tribunal framed issues, recorded evidence of claimant as PW-1 and Dr.Chidambar D.
Kulkarni as PW-2 and Exhibits P1 to P11 were marked.

In rebuttal, official of insurer was examined as RW-1 and got marked Exhibits R1 to R4.
7.

On consideration, tribunal answered issue no.1 partly in affirmative, issue no.2 in affirmative,
issue no.3 in negative and issue no.4 by allowing claim petition in part and granting compensation of Rs.2,16,000/- with interest at rate of 9% per annum and holding claimant who have contributed to an extent of 50% to accident and therefore denying compensation to said extent.
8. Not satisfied with quantum and liability, claimant is in appeal.
9. Sri. Neel P Patil, learned counsel appearing for claimant - appellant submitted that claimant was a pillion rider on motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-24-J-3249, which belonging to owner.
Since claimant was not rider of either of two motorcycles involved in accident, there was absolutely no justification for tribunal denying compensation to extent of 50%.

sentences.text: It was submitted that claimant aged 22 years, working as agriculturist sustained fracture of left inter trachea of femur.
PW-2 assessed disability caused due to said injury at 30% in relation to left lower limb and consequent loss of earning capacity.
Therefore, assessment of loss of earning capacity was on lower side.

11. It was submitted that though claimant had stated that he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month from agriculture, tribunal considered it at Rs.5,000/- per month which was inadequate and sought enhancement.
12.
On other hand, Sri S.V. Yaji, learned counsel appearing for insurer supported award and opposed appeal.
13. From above submissions, occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent riding of offending motorcycle by its rider, claimant sustained injuries and permanent disability is not in dispute.

Tribunal assessed compensation and held insurer liable to pay compensation.
14.
Only claimant is in appeal challenging said award.

15. Therefore, only point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
16.
Insofar as monthly income, though claimant stated that he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month from agriculture, same is not substantiated with any evidence.
In absence, tribunal was justified in assessing it notionally.
Notional income for period 2011 is Rs.6,000/-.
Therefore, tribunal was not justified in taking it at Rs.5,000/-.

17. Insofar as loss of earning capacity, PW-2 - Dr.Chidambar D. Kulkarni upon clinical examination held that claimant had sustained disability to extent of 30% to limb, but he did not assess loss of earning capacity.

Considering nature of injury and disability sustained in light of occupation, tribunal assessed loss of earning capacity at 10%
which appears to be just and proper.

Thus, future loss of income would be as follows:
Rs.6,000,/- X 10% X 12 X 18 = Rs.1,29,600/-.
18.

It is seen that tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.33,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.15,000/- towards future amenities, Rs.10,000/- towards life expectancy and Rs.5,000/- towards conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges, which appear to be just and proper.
19. Considering lay off period of three months, tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of income during said period.
Since income is reassessed at Rs.6,000/- compensation would be Rs.18,000/-.

Thus, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

15. However, in view of recent decision of this Court in case of Shriram General Insurance Company Limited, Rajasthan V/s Smt.Laxmi and others reported in (2018) 8 AKR 808, interest awardable in a claim petition under Motor Vehicles Act, cannot be more than 6%.

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance Company Limited, Rajasthan V/s Smt.Laxmi and others reported in (2018) 8 AKR 808
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, rate of interest awarded by tribunal is reduced to 6%.
21. Insofar as contributory negligence, it is seen that claimant was pillion rider.
Accident is caused due to negligence of riders of both motorcycles, which would be composite negligence.

As per Full Bench decision of this Court in case of Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation, by its Managing Director v/s Aran @ Aravind and Ors., reported in 2003 SCC OnLine Kar 715, held that claimant would be entitled to claim entire compensation either of joint tortfeasors and denied of compensation to extent of 50% would not be justified.
Therefore, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

22. Consequently, I pass following:
- 10 -  O R D E R  i. Appeal is allowed in part.
